stem.en: Two ships meet head-on at night in open water. What should each ship do?

feedback.en: Turning left would bring them across each other's path. The rule is to turn right.
Yes. Each ship turns to its own right, and they pass left side to left side.
Two ships holding course head-on will collide.
Stopping is not the rule, and it does not get either ship out of the way.

explanation.en: When two ships meet head-on, both have to act. Each turns to its own right, so the two pass left side to left side, which sailors call port to port.

hints.en: This is the one meeting where both ships do the same thing.
